A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a MSC-derived product (Exo-dMAPPs) which is able to attenuate chronic airway inflammation through the modulation of immunoregulatory cells in the lungs of CS-exposed mice as well as COPD patients.

the beneficial effects of Exo-d-MAPS in attenuation of chronic airways inflammation are due to the immunomodulatory properties of this product, which is mediated by the expansion of alternatively activated macrophage, regulatory DCs and T regulatory cells in the lung.

Exo-dMAPPS, which contains immunomodulatory proteins derived from MSCs, attenuates chronic airway inflammation through the modulation of the immunosuppressive and inflammatory properties of lung-inflitrated macrophages.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the beneficial effects of Exo-d-MAPS are the consequence of a complex interaction of multiple paracrine factors that are able to suppress the production of proinflammatory mediators and to expand immunoregulatory cells.
the MSCs-derived paracrine product Exo-d-MAPPs is a promising candidate for treatment of chronic inflammatory airway diseases.
MSCs can be used as a new therapeutic agent, and MSC-derived products, such as Exo-d-MAPS, can be used as an alternative to cell-based therapy.
